title: Pilot acceptance decision, DPA exceptions & pricing pathway
summary: Redwood and Veridian reviewed pilot acceptance criteria, DPA exception requests for data residency, and pricing pathways tied to committed volume.
Key legal asks: explicit egress fee cap, KMS integration details, and SOC2 / ISO attestation timeline.
Technical checks: VPC peering vs private endpoint, latency SLOs for the triage flow, and a short benchmarking window requested by Cloud Architecture.
Next steps agreed: Redwood to send redlines and updated pricing worksheet; Veridian legal to indicate DPA exception priority by next Tuesday.
topics: Pilot acceptance criteria and signoff process
DPA exceptions for EU data residency and cross-border transfer
SLA thresholds and egress fee caps
Pricing path: hosted credits, reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go
Security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence timeline
action_items: Michael Chen: draft MSA redline focusing on egress cap + pilot termination clause - due 2025-06-24
Sara Patel: assemble latency and throughput benchmark plan + test harness link - due 2025-06-22
Damien Lee: package SOC2 report and compliance pack, include attestation dates - due 2025-06-23
Lena Ortiz: confirm which DPA exceptions are must-haves vs nice-to-have, share prioritized list - due 2025-06-24
Ravi Srinivasan: run initial connectivity check of VPC peering and share traceroutes - due 2025-06-21
next_steps: Redwood to send updated MSA/DPA redlines and pricing worksheet (hosted vs dedicated scenarios)
Veridian legal to return prioritized DPA exceptions and any alternative controls that would be acceptable
SE team to run 48-hour benchmark with Veridian sample prompt set and return results
Schedule follow-up decision call next Thursday (2025-06-26) to confirm pilot go/no-go
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~1h14m
Attendees: Michael (Redwood AE), Sara (Redwood SE), Damien (Redwood CSM); Jason (Veridian Procurement), Lena (Veridian Legal), Ravi (Veridian Cloud), Aisha (PM)

Summary / quick notes: we spent first 20 minutes on legal asks, then technical gating items; some cross-talk when we discussed egress math.

[00:00:08] Michael (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Jason, Lena, Ravi — good to see you. Quick agenda — legal redlines and DPA exceptions, SLA and egress, KMS, then a short technical bench plan.

[00:00:25] Jason (Veridian): Thanks. We've got procurement and legal here, we need clarity on egress and committed discounts, otherwise the PO team can't route. Also, DPA exceptions: we need EU residency for PII and a carve-out for telemetry.

[00:00:48] Lena (Legal): Yeah, and to be super clear, we are not comfortable with open cross-border transfer without supplemental safeguards. We listed some exceptions in the packet we sent yesterday.

[00:01:10] Michael: Got it. We reviewed that packet. There are three paths: 1) Hosted with data residency controls and regional model pinning, 2) Dedicated reserved capacity that keeps KV cache and logs in your VPC, 3) Private deployment on-prem. Each has tradeoffs on cost and time to production.

[00:01:33] Sara (SE): To add, for the triage flow you're planning we can Hit the latency SLO of sub-200ms for short prompts with Dedicated in most regions; hosted can be similar if you pin region and model variant. But egress math differs.

[00:01:52] Ravi (Cloud): Can you explain egress math again? Our finance team wants an example for 10M tokens / month.

[00:02:05] Michael: Sure — broadly, token costs + egress (data transfer out). We can cap egress for the pilot and include a per-GB cap in the MSA. Example: with committed usage, we can offer an egress cap of $0.05/GB up to X GB, then a stepped rate. We need to put numbers in the worksheet.

[00:02:29] Jason: The ask is an absolute cap for the pilot so finance can sign. If it's open-ended we hit a hard stop.

[00:02:41] Lena: We also want an explicit right to terminate the pilot without penalty if an incident occurs or if data residency is violated.

[00:02:50] Michael: That's reasonable for a pilot. We usually allow a 30-day termination window for pilots with no early termination fee; in production contracts there are different commitments. I'll flag that in the MSA redline.

[00:03:10] Sara: One more note: KMS — we support bring-your-own-key via our KMS integration (HSM-backed) for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via a cloud KMS integration, but there are nuances around key-lifetime and replay logs.

[00:03:33] Ravi: For Veridian we need CMK in our cloud account and support for key rotation without rekeying the entire model state. Is that supported?

[00:03:42] Sara: We support rewrapping the KV cache and metadata; full model re-encryption isn't required. There are performance implications for rotation windows but we can share specifics.

[00:04:02] Aisha (PM): Quick process question — what does signoff look like? Is procurement the final approver or do we need an Exec sponsor?

[00:04:12] Jason: Procurement will approve the PO if legal signs off on the MSA/DPA. Finance will sign the PO once pricing and caps are clear. Exec signoff only if we exceed X spend or multi-region.

[00:04:31] Lena: On the DPA — we can accept some exceptions if there are compensating controls, e.g., specific audit logging, field-level pseudonymization, and SLA-backed removal windows.

[00:04:48] Michael: Okay, so action for legal: can you prioritize the DPA exception list into must-haves vs nice-to-haves? We'll respond with alternative controls and language.

[00:05:05] Lena: We'll do that.

[00:05:14] Damien (CSM): On the compliance pack — we will send SOC2 type II report and the ISO cert copy. Damien to own that.

[00:05:22] Michael: Great. Switching to SLA specifics — what does Veridian need for uptime and latency SLO?

[00:05:31] Ravi: For the triage path we need 99.5% availability and p95 latency under 300ms for the short prompt set. For the model training/eval runs we don't need that tight SLO.

[00:05:44] Sara: 99.5% is doable in Dedicated with our autoscale and burst policies; hosted for pilot we can aim for 99.0% with monitoring and fallbacks. For latency p95 300ms — depends on length distribution and KV size; we should run a 48-hour bench with sample data.

[00:06:05] Ravi: We'll provide the sample prompt set and expected QPS.

[00:06:12] Michael: Perfect. We'll map the SLO language in the SLA section. Also, we need to clarify incident response timelines and escalation contacts — we'll add a 1-hour P1 response target for the pilot.

[00:06:28] Jason: That's acceptable. Now pricing: we want a committed pilot price and conversion path to production pricing. Our concern is sticker shock if the pilot scales and costs spike.

[00:06:39] Michael: Understandable. For pilot we'll propose a fixed credit package that covers X tokens / month for three months at a discount; if you convert to reserved capacity we give deeper unit discounts and an egress cap. I'll include conversion credits in the worksheet.

[00:06:55] Jason: Will you include examples for 2 consumption buckets? Low (<=2M tokens) and High (>=10M tokens)?

[00:07:04] Michael: Yes, we'll provide both bands and the breakpoint where reserved capacity becomes cost-effective.

[00:07:12] Lena: We also need to see indemnity language around data breach and data residency.

[00:07:18] Michael: We have standard clauses but we'll propose a pilot-limited indemnity and a separate production indemnity. We'll mark that in the redline.

[00:07:30] Sara: Technical detail to note — KV cache persistence in Dedicated means metadata stays in Veridian's VPC, but some telemetry metrics are still aggregated to Redwood telemetry for platform health. We can restrict telemetry fields for the pilot.

[00:07:49] Ravi: That's important. We want telemetry limited to non-PII and aggregated counts only.

[00:07:56] Michael: We'll propose a telemetry whitelist and include it as an appendix to the DPA.

[00:08:05] Aisha: About timelines — if we get MSA redlines back by next Wednesday can we start the bench the following Monday?

[00:08:12] Sara: Tentatively yes, the SE team can stand up a short test harness in your region. We will need access for a service account and a short IP allowlist for the VPC peer.

[00:08:25] Ravi: We'll bind the service account to a role with least privilege. Also want to run a quick connectivity check this week.

[00:08:34] Sara: Great, we'll share the connectivity checklist after this call.

[00:08:40] Michael: Let's surface some of the tricky DPA asks now so we know where to focus legal redlines — Lena, can you call out the top three?

[00:08:48] Lena: Top three: 1) EU residency for PII with no transfer outside EU (exceptions require SCCs or equivalent safeguards), 2) eDiscovery and deletion timing (30 days for user-requested deletion), and 3) stronger audit rights and on-demand right-to-audit language.

[00:09:09] Michael: OK that's helpful. For #1 we can support regional processing and model pinning for outputs; for transfers we can propose SCCs plus a technical control of encrypting in-region with CMK. For #2 30-day window is reasonable for pilot if we get acceptance on scope; for #3 we can offer read-only audit logs and an SLA'd window for delivering logs.

[00:09:33] Jason: On deletion semantics, does deletion also purge cached KV within the timeline or is that longer?

[00:09:41] Sara: We can purge KV for entries tied to a user identifier on request; metadata snapshots might remain for a short retention used for debugging, but we can minimize that and document the retention windows.

[00:09:56] Ravi: Anything about model fine-tuning and derivative models? We do not want our customer data included in any public model re-training.

[00:10:04] Michael: We never train public models with customer production data. We'll include explicit language prohibiting use of your data for model training without consent.

[00:10:14] Damien: Also we'll log a commitment: no external sharing of training datasets; will be in the DPA clause.

[00:10:20] Lena: Good. Back to practicalities: procurement wants a single consolidated worksheet with three pricing scenarios, and a separate one-page summary for finance.

[00:10:29] Michael: We'll prepare both. Damien will own the finance summary.

[00:10:34] Damien: Yep, I got it.

[00:10:38] [.. call continues ..]

[00:20:12] [00:20:12] Sara: Quick tech note — we'll need a small sample corpus for the bench (5000 prompts). That helps simulate token distribution and KV cache hit rates.

[00:20:27] Ravi: We'll drop that into the secure share. Expect it by 2025-06-20 EOD.

[00:20:35] Michael: Timeline recap: Redwood to send redline and pricing sheet by 2025-06-24; Veridian to prioritize DPA exceptions by the same date; SE bench to run 48 hours once connectivity is validated (estimated 2025-06-30). Follow-up decision call 2025-06-26.

[00:20:56] Jason: That matches expectations. One open flag — can Redwood guarantee a pilot egress cap that procurement can accept?

[00:21:06] Michael: For the pilot we can accept a fixed-dollar cap tied to the credit package. We'll show a worked example in the worksheet. For production, egress is handled under reserved capacity pricing with caps available on request.

[00:21:20] Lena: We'll take the worksheet to procurement and finance; expect questions.

[00:21:26] Aisha: Any outstanding technical blockers?

[00:21:30] Sara: None critical; just connectivity, service account, and the bench dataset. We'll need the VPC allowlist info.

[00:21:38] Ravi: We'll provide the allowlist and run a basic traceroute today.

[00:21:46] Michael: Great. Last bit — indemnity and insurance: we have our standard limits; if you require higher insurance limits for pilot we'll note that and escalate.

[00:21:58] Jason: For pilot standard limits are fine, production we might require higher.

[00:22:05] Michael: Understood. Okay, quick recap and owners — I'll send the MSA/DPA redline and the pricing workbook; Sara will send the connectivity checklist and bench plan; Damien will share SOC2/ISO docs; Lena will prioritize DPA exceptions. Schedule decision call for 2025-06-26. Anything else?

[00:22:26] Lena: One more: please include a clear rollback/cleanup clause for the pilot — how do you remove data at the end of the pilot.

[00:22:35] Michael: We'll add a cleanup appendix with retention windows and a verified deletion process.

[00:22:42] Jason: Thanks everyone. We'll push internally and get the DPA priorities back by 6/24.

[00:22:49] Michael: Thanks all, we'll send the redlines and the worksheet early next week. Meeting adjourned.

[00:23:00] -- End of call export (transcription may contain minor errors: e.g., K V cache sometimes written as "K V cache" or "K-V cache").
